708700.t: From Proto-Hellenic *méli, from Proto-Indo-European *mélit (“honey”). Cognates include Mycenaean Greek 𐀕𐀪 (me-ri), Latin mel, Gothic 𐌼𐌹𐌻𐌹𐌸 (miliþ), and Old Armenian մեղր (mełr).

708722.t: From μελῳδός (melōidós, “musical”) + -ία (-ía), from μέλος (mélos) "musical phrase" + ᾠδή (ōidḗ), contracted form of ἀοιδή (aoidḗ) "song".

708752.t: From Proto-Hellenic *(h)méros; equivalent to μερ- (mer-), the root of μείρομαι (meíromai, “to receive as one's portion”) + -ος (-os).

708768.t: From Proto-Hellenic *métsos, from Proto-Indo-European *médʰyos (“between”). Cognate with Latin medius, Sanskrit मध्य (madhya), Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬌𐬜𐬌𐬌𐬁𐬥𐬀 (maⁱδiiāna), Old Armenian մէջ (mēǰ), etc.

708780.t: Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀕𐀲 (me-ta); further derivation is uncertain.

708702.t: Potentially haplologized from *μελιλίχια (*melĭlĭ́khĭă), from Proto-Indo-European *mélit (“honey”) + *leyǵʰ- (“lick”). Compare Albanian bletë and Sanskrit मधुलिह् (madhulih).

708728.t: Sometimes derived from a Proto-Indo-European *me(-)mbʰ-e-, and compared with obsolete English mump (“to cheat, swindle”), Gothic 𐌱𐌹𐌼𐌰𐌼𐍀𐌾𐌰𐌽 (bimampjan, “to mock”).

708736.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ménō, from Proto-Indo-European *men- (“to stay, stand still”). Cognates include Latin maneō (“remain”), Persian ماندن (mândan, “to remain”).

708707.t: Likely from a Proto-Indo-European *mel- (“limb”); compare Breton mell (“joint”), Cornish mal (“id”), Welsh cymmal (“id”), which are from Proto-Celtic *melsā (“knuckle”).

708705.t: Of uncertain origin. Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *mel- (“to linger, hesitate, be late”), and connected with Latin prōmellō (“to postpone a court case”), Old Irish mall (“slow, tardy”).

708777.t: Uncertain; possibly from Proto-Indo-European *med- (“to measure”) or *med- (“to be full”), the latter comparable to Sanskrit मत्त (mattá, “drunk, intoxicated”).

708746.t: Deverbative of μέριμνα (mérimna, “anxiety, concern”). Cognates include Latin memor and Sanskrit स्मरति (smarati, “to think, to recollect”)

708784.t: From μεταβάλλω (metabállō, “to change”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix).

708745.t: From Proto-Hellenic *mérimnā, probably from Proto-Indo-European *(s)mer- (“to remember”). Cognate with μέρμερος (mérmeros, “anxious”), Old English ġemimor (“mindful, remembering”) and Latin memor (“mindful”).

708756.t: Almost certainly a technical word of Pre-Greek origin, because of the many different variants.

708782.t: From μετα- (meta-, “concerning change of”) + βάλλω (bállō, “to throw”).

708749.t: μερίζω (merízō, “to divide”) + -μός (-mós, event or process noun suffix)
